plain_english_policy: This bill removes a historical legal barrier to prosecuting homicide cases in Alabama where the victim's death occurs more than one year and one day after the initial act that caused it. It explicitly overrides the common law 'year-and-a-day rule,' which historically prevented prosecution if death took longer than this period—even when the cause was clearly criminal (e.g., poisoning, torture, or delayed injuries).
policy_direction_if_enacted: The enactment of HB484 would shift Alabama’s homicide prosecutions toward a **prosecutorial advantage** by eliminating a procedural defense that could otherwise acquit defendants in cases where death was foreseeable but delayed. This aligns with modern legal trends favoring victim protection over technicalities, though it does not alter substantive guilt or punishment—only the timing of prosecution. The bill’s naming as 'The Officer Tommy Bishop Act' suggests it may have been tailored to address a specific case (e.g., where the year-and-a-day rule blocked justice).
sponsorship_supports_position: The bill’s text and title explicitly advance a policy of **expanding prosecutorial power** by removing a procedural barrier to conviction. No ideological inference beyond the bill’s language is warranted.
evidence_quotes: It shall not be a defense or a bar to a prosecution for criminal homicide if the commission of the act... occurred more than one year and one day before the death of the victim.
This section shall apply to any act or acts occurring after July 1, 2010.
